title: Mama Jasinta
about: A tribute to the person who welcomed newcomers and made State Arts-In feel like home.
description: This track honors Mama Jasinta, whose kindness and guidance helped new participants find their place. From teaching hidden shortcuts and backstage paths to showing where to eat, rest, and belong, she quietly became a mentor to countless first-timers. It's a song about the people who make an unfamiliar place feel like family.
lyrics: Like we'd never cross them all.
She just waved and said, "Come on."
Then led us through a doorway
We didn't know was there at all.
And everything the old hands knew.
We came in as scattered strangers,
She showed us where the cheap food was,
How to cross a crowded fair
Ten minutes through the side ways,
While the public moved an hour,
Past the rooms behind the rooms,
Up the stairs and toward the towers.
The green room and the light shelf,
And the places we could rest.
She taught us how to make it
Through the long and sleepless days,
How to laugh when things went sideways
And everything the old hands knew.
We came in as scattered strangers,
No one handed her the name.
You made the strange place feel like home.
With a trail of little ducklings
Every year the fair moved on,
But the paths you showed the new kids
Stayed long after you were gone.
